newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weak Europe cocoa grinds mask positive 1996 - trader.
newsitem.headline: Weak Europe cocoa grinds mask positive 1996 - trader.

text.p: Lower British and German cocoa grind results in fourth quarter 1996 distracted from an overall gain by seven percent in Britain, Germany and the Netherlands, a weekly market report from German trader Albrecht & Dill said.
The trader said markets mostly ignored the weaker trend in two of the leading European chocolate producing countries and the modest rise in the Dutch result.
The Dutch quarterly figure was up 3.9 percent on the same 1995 period at 97,273, Britain's was down 3.3 percent at 45,147 tonnes and Germany's down sharply by 21.2 percent at 56,255.
A&D said capacity shifts at cocoa processing plants and several days of strike action over sick pay at German confectionery plants in early December were to blame.
Cocoa prices were presently unattractive to German consumers because of a high sterling/mark ratio, A&D also noted. London cocoa futures are denominated in sterling.
Prices were two to three percent above buyers' ideas here, it said.
Turning to fundamentals, A&D said current Ivory Coast port arrivals were estimated at 600,000 tonnes, some 100,000 tonne below the same 1996 date.
